guards.what: G3 (LIVE): the copy is rebuilt from the card id, where C# clones the actual card instance
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): `create_clone` (cards/base.py) IS a memberwise copy now. `ClonePreservingMutability` is `AbstractModel.MutableClone` (a MemberwiseClone) and only THEN `DeepCloneFields` (CardModel.cs:1193-1216) and `AfterCloned` (:1218-1239), so the sim opens with `clone.__dict__.update(card.__dict__)` and the two override passes only re-point what must not be shared (`combat`, and the enchantment/affliction that DeepCloneFields re-creates). Everything the guard named now rides along: the LIVE KEYWORD SET (`_keywords = GetKeywordsWithSources(KeywordSources.Local)`, :1196-1200 -- Music Box's Ethereal), the cloned `_energyCost` and its `_localModifiers` (:1202 -> CardEnergyCost.cs:411-421 -- SetThisCombat, AddThisTurn, free-this-turn), the cloned `_dynamicVars` (:1201 -- a grown Rampage clones grown) and `BaseReplayCount` (Hidden Gem). `CreateClone`'s own tail, `ExhaustOnNextPlay = false` (:2178), is the last line. ONE MORE FINDING, and it is the reason the fix could not be a one-liner: DeepCloneFields re-attaches with `EnchantInternal` (:1204-1209 -> :1491-1498), which checks NO CanEnchant and does NOT run `ModifyCard` -- EnchantmentModel.cs:350-353 says why in as many words, "It is NOT called when a card is cloned, because the enchantment's effects will already be reflected in the card's values." The sim only had the normal `attach`, and re-running it on a memberwise copy is not merely redundant, it THROWS for Souls, whose CanEnchant demands the Exhaust its own ModifyCard removes. `Enchantment.attach_internal` is that path. EXECUTED, old -> new: keyword False->True, free-this-turn cost 1->0, base_replay_count 0->3, a twice-played Rampage 9->19. Pinned by test/test_create_clone_memberwise.py. TEST MOVED (non-negotiable 5): test_card_clone_enchantment.py's `test_clone_reapplies_a_static_card_modification` is now `test_clone_carries_a_static_card_modification`, with the reason inline; its assertion is unchanged. NOT CLOSED: nothing at this site.  The text it replaced read: NARROWED 2026-07-27, RE-OPENED 2026-07-28: the copy carries more than it used to but it is still REBUILT from the class, which is exactly what this guard claims. CLOSED: sts2_rl/relics/burning_sticks.py calls `create_clone(card)` (sts2_rl/cards/base.py:57-83), so the copy now carries the source's upgrade level plus live copies of its ENCHANTMENT and AFFLICTION -- an enchanted Defend no longer clones as `clone.enchantment=None`. STILL OPEN: create_clone opens with `clone = type(card)()` (cards/base.py:74). BurningSticks.cs:44-52 calls card.CreateClone(), a memberwise MutableClone whose DeepCloneFields (CardModel.cs:1193-1216) also carries `_keywords` (Local sources), `_dynamicVars`, `_energyCost` and `_temporaryStarCosts`. EXECUTED 2026-07-28 (same probe as relic/music_box G1): a source with set_cost_this_combat(0), base_replay_count 1 and is_ethereal True clones to (energy_cost 1, replay 0, ethereal False). LIVE ROUTE FOR A SKILL, which is all this relic ever copies: potions.py, relics/crossbow.py, relics/jeweled_mask.py, relics/vexing_puzzlebox.py and cards/infernal_blade.py all call set_free_this_turn / set_cost_this_combat, so a cost-reduced Skill that is then exhausted returns to hand at FULL cost in the sim and at the modified cost in the game. One mechanism with relic/music_box G1 (binding rule 3); the fix is in create_clone, not in either relic. WAS: the port built `make_card(card.id)` and replayed only the upgrade level. guards.what: G2: sweep-upgrade flags burning_sticks.py:24 as an unguarded `Card.upgrade()` (PROMPT.md bug class 14) -- settled by execution as a false positive
guards.rationale: The call is `for _ in range(card.upgrade_level): clone.upgrade()`, so the loop count is the ORIGINAL's own upgrade level and the clone is the same card id with the same max_upgrade_level -- it can never be pushed past a level the original legitimately holds, which is exactly what C#'s CardCmd.Upgrade IsUpgradable check (CardModel.cs:785-789) prevents. On top of that the relic only ever clones Skills (burning_sticks.py:25 `card.card_type != CardType.SKILL`). EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/relic_probes.py batch3`): the max_upgrade_level==0 population is {CURSE: 18, STATUS: 14, QUEST: 3} and `SKILL cards with max_upgrade_level==0: []`. Recorded rather than dropped because content-relic-sweeps.md sweep D lists this site as unaudited batch work; it is now cleared.

The `player != base.Owner` / `card.Owner != base.Owner` / `participants.Contains(base.Owner.Creature)` family is the multiplayer per-player filter on a hook the game dispatches for every player (and, for the participants form, also admits pets). The sim is single-player by construction (one RunState, one PlayerCombatState) and models no pet creature, so the filter is structurally satisfied. Multiplayer-only paths are out of scope under the shared contract.

Neither codebase reads it here -- C# names the parameter and ignores it, and the sim's on_card_exhausted(card) has no such argument. Checked because relic/charons_ashes in the same batch also takes and ignores it (`bool _`), so an ethereal exhaust triggers both relics on both sides.

guards.what: N2: C# sets WasUsedThisCombat AFTER AddGeneratedCardToCombat (BurningSticks.cs:50-52); the sim sets it BEFORE (burning_sticks.py:29-33)
guards.rationale: The ordering only matters under re-entrancy: if adding the clone could itself exhaust a Skill, C# would recurse once and the sim would not. CardPileCmd.add_to_hand (cmds.py:500-514) appends and fires _enter_combat; no ported on-enter effect exhausts a card, so the two orderings are indistinguishable today -- and the sim's is the safer one. Recorded because the flag is the same field guard G1 is about.
